title.narrative: Free Nutritious Meals Programme: Managing Catering Resources in professional kitchens to reduce food waste

description.narrative:
Indonesia has committed to supporting the Sustainable Development Goals and greenhouse gas emission reduction targets following the Paris Agreement in 2030. To live up to that Indonesia has to tackle and reduce their issue with generating large amounts of food loss and waste (FLW), which has a negative impact on living up to the Paris Agreement. As it is of now there is being generated 115-184 kg FLW pr capita pr year and Indonesia is also claimed to be the second largest FLW producing country in the world per capita. Because of this the National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas) has started working with new strategies and plans to support initiatives reducing FLW.
The focus on reducing FLW plays a role in The Free Nutritious Meals Programme (FNMP), that President Prabowo has formalized under Presidential Regulation and is a major national initiative of the government of Indonesia. The program aims to benefit 82 million pre-school and school children, as well as pregnant and breastfeeding women with one meal per day. The FNMP reflects Indonesia’s commitment to addressing malnutrition and delivering economic and social development. However, the environmental risks associated with the FNMP, particularly food and packaging waste generated by mass catering, remain under-addressed. And for a country that already produce a large amount of FLW, the FNMP has a big change of increase the amount of FLW further.
The purpose of creating a guidance for inventory (ordering food, storage of it, stock control and so on) and teaching materials to the units is to help support the units’ staff to be able to make decisions that reduce food waste. And with this it will be possible to design management tools, that can support the work which Bappenas, NNA and National Food Agency (NFA) are doing in finding solutions for reducing food waste in the FNMP.
